item.title: Playground
item.description:
Playground #

Search the teaching dataset right on this page — the Pizza engine compiled to WebAssembly runs in your browser, and nothing you type leaves the page. Queries use Pizza’s canonical DSL, and the results are engine-level output (no gateway envelope: no _key, _shards or _collection wrappers; the engine’s parsed_query plan string appears only behind the result panel’s debug 🐛 toggle).

Flip the editor to SQL to run SELECT statements through the engine’s SQL frontend — the same parse/lower/shape path the /_sql gateway wire rides. The example chips load per-dataset statements covering the subset (filters, MATCH/SCORE()/HIGHLIGHT, KNN, CASE, scalar functions, GROUP BY with DATE_TRUNC/HISTOGRAM bucketing, COUNT(DISTINCT), $1 parameters, an EXPLAIN chip showing the compiled DSL plan — and one deliberately rejected statement to show a positioned plan error). SQL answers render as the gateway’s frozen columns/rows envelope — a typed table, with a raw JSON view one click away. The composite cursor walk chip shows keyset paging: a full grouped page hands back a cursor, and Next page resubmits the identical statement with it — exactly what /_sql’s cursor request field does.
